title: MyRecon vs SpiderFoot: Browser vs Suite | MyRecon
description: Compare MyRecon fast browser handle and breach checks against SpiderFoot 200+ module automated OSINT scans, local hosting and analyst scope.
h1: MyRecon vs SpiderFoot: instant handle checks vs 200+ modules
intro: SpiderFoot is a self-hosted automated OSINT framework built around more than 200 data-collection modules for infrastructure, threat intelligence, and target correlation. MyRecon focuses on zero-setup browser and mobile checks for public handles, breaches, and domain triage. Comparing them clarifies when a full suite helps versus when it slows you down.

sections.heading: Target scope: single-question triage vs 200+ modules
sections.body: SpiderFoot accepts domains, IP blocks, ASNs, emails, phone numbers, and names, chaining 200+ passive and active modules into correlation graphs. MyRecon narrows the surface to rapid handle checks, email breach lookups, k-anonymity password checks, RDAP, DNS, and IP context without provisioning a scan workspace.

sections.heading: Hosting overhead and API key management
sections.body: Running open-source SpiderFoot (smicallef/spiderfoot) requires hosting a Python 3 service locally or on a server and supplying third-party API keys for services like Shodan, Censys, or VirusTotal to unlock deeper modules. MyRecon runs immediately in any browser or on Android with no server maintenance.

sections.heading: Attack-surface correlation versus self-audit speed
sections.body: Security teams mapping an entire corporate domain benefit from SpiderFoot's automated DNS brute-forcing, certificate transparency mining, and threat-feed enrichment. Individuals auditing a handful of personal aliases or checking whether an email appeared in a breach avoid hours of noisy module tuning by starting in MyRecon.

sections.heading: Noise control and evidence verification
sections.body: Multi-module suites can generate thousands of low-confidence events if broad passive modules trigger together without strict filters. MyRecon keeps handle verdicts segmented into found, not_found, and unknown so blocked platforms never masquerade as clean absences or verified hits.

faq.question: Does SpiderFoot replace a dedicated social handle checker?
faq.answer: SpiderFoot includes social account modules, yet its primary strength lies in infrastructure, threat feeds, and domain attack-surface correlation across 200+ connectors rather than high-signal consumer self-audits.

faq.question: Why does SpiderFoot require third-party API keys for many checks?
faq.answer: Many SpiderFoot modules act as orchestration wrappers around external intelligence providers such as Shodan, Censys, or Have I Been Pwned, requiring your own API credentials to query those services.

faq.question: Is SpiderFoot free to run locally?
faq.answer: Yes. The open-source SpiderFoot repository on GitHub is free to self-host with Python 3, though optional commercial threat feeds require paid API plans from their respective vendors.

faq.question: Which tool is better for checking a domain and handle in under a minute?
faq.answer: MyRecon finishes quick RDAP, DNS, IP, and handle checks in seconds without deploying a local web server, while SpiderFoot is better suited to multi-hour infrastructure reconnaissance.

benchmark.summary: SpiderFoot and MyRecon target different operational layers: SpiderFoot orchestrates 200+ infrastructure and threat-intelligence modules from a self-hosted workspace, whereas MyRecon delivers lightweight browser and Android triage with zero server setup.

pros: No Python server, database workspace, or third-party API key setup required
Cleaner workflow for quick personal footprint, breach, and handle verification
Mobile-ready via Google Play alongside desktop browser access
cons: Does not orchestrate 200+ automated Shodan, ASN, or dark-web threat-intel modules
No interactive SQLite correlation graph across enterprise CIDR ranges
migration_note: Deploy SpiderFoot when conducting authorized enterprise attack-surface mapping with external API keys; choose MyRecon whenever you want instant browser or Android checks without managing a reconnaissance daemon. Note that SpiderFoot is occasionally misspelled as spidefoot or spiderfot; verify the official smicallef/spiderfoot repository before cloning.
